messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Routing subsystem detected sustained p99 token-latency > 5s (SLO breach) for streaming RPCs in us-west-2. Auto-escalating to on-call. Links: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/4032109999 , runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/routing-tail

pagerduty-bot: Paging sara (oncall) — incident assigned. Pager: PD-83421.

sara: ack. jumping on it now. grabbing current dashboard.

sara: quick summary from dashboards: p95 ~ 900ms, p99 ~ 6.2s for streaming endpoints. Error rate low but client-side stall observed for chunk streaming. Throughput steady.

jonathan: FYI I just saw a spike in cross-zone reroutes in the router logs around the same time. Could be a policy loop causing hot partitions. pulling router logs.

sara: can you paste the recent router.trace for a hot client id?

jonathan: pastebin: ```
# router.trace snippet
2026-03-15T14:02:03Z route_request id=abc123 client=svc-stream shard=42 -> backend=pool-A
2026-03-15T14:02:03Z route_request id=abc123 client=svc-stream shard=42 -> backend=pool-B (fallback)
2026-03-15T14:02:04Z cache_miss kv_prefix client=svc-stream key=ctx:abc123
2026-03-15T14:02:08Z long-tail token_emit latency=5.8s path=pool-B
```

tina: looks like some requests are being bounced between pools A/B due to an aggressive "prefer-local" weight update we rolled out earlier today.

ben: I noticed a rollout for routing.policy.v2 at 13:55 UTC which touched prefer_local weight heuristics. Could be the culprit.

sara: mitigation idea: rollback the routing.policy.v2 weights to previous stable config and observe. Can someone run the rollback? This is allowed per runbook.

jonathan: prepping rollback. command: `kubectl -n routing apply -f /configs/routing/weights/v1-weights.yaml` — will also restart router-config watcher.

sara: do it, but first add a temporary short-circuit: increase eager-fallback cooldown to 30s so we don't oscillate. config path: `/configs/routing/weights/overrides.json`

jonathan: applied cooldown override. rolling weights back now. will post when done.

pagerduty-bot: sara acknowledged incident. Estimated impact window started 2026-03-15T14:02:00Z.

jonathan: rollback applied at 14:08 UTC. router-config-watchers restarted.

sara: seeing immediate drop in cross-zone reroutes in the heatmap. p99 dropping from 6.2s -> 1.4s in the next 2 minutes. trending down.

lucas: nice. any customer-impact notes? which customers affected?

tina: customer telemetry: a subset of streaming customers experienced stall/resume behavior — chunk ACKs delayed but final responses succeeded. No sustained user-visible 5xxs logged. Customer support IDs: CS-3321, CS-3329.

sara: good to know. marking degraded for streaming SLOs but no data-loss. I'm going to open an incident bridge for postmortem. ops-bridge: https://zoom.redwood/ops/4032109999

ben: question: why did prefer-local weights cause oscillation? My initial hypothesis: hot partition (shard 42) was being detected, weight moved to local nodes then autoscaler/eviction changed backend availability causing handoffs. That creates repeated fallback which increases latency.

jonathan: log excerpt shows fallback to pool-B after cache miss which incurred big KV fetch. If the KV fetch depends on cross-pool metadata, that amplifies tail latency.

sara: action items: (1) create rollback PR audit (jonathan) (2) throttle prefer-local weight rollout until we have heatmap tests (ben) (3) reach out to CS for impacted customers and offer post-incident note (tina) (4) schedule a follow-up with routing runtime + infra to add more robust cooldown metrics (lucas).

jonathan: I've opened PR 4829 with rollback details and postmortem placeholders.

tina: contacting CS for affected customers now. sending templated note: "We observed increased streaming stalls for customers using chunked streams in us-west-2 between 14:02-14:10 UTC; mitigation performed and system back to normal. Follow-up postmortem to come."

sara: handing incident to lucas for post-incident & long tail analysis. lucas, please take over the bridge. I'm going offline in 10.

lucas: taking over. joining ops-bridge. summary for handoff: p99 tail spike due to routing weight rollout -> oscillation between pools -> KV cache misses -> cross-pool fallbacks -> streaming stalls. Mitigated by rollback + cooldown override at ~14:08 UTC. Current status: recovering, p99 ~ 1.2s, p95 ~ 800ms.

lucas: next steps I'll own: collect request traces for hot shards, reproduce policy in staging with synthetic hotkey, and schedule a sit-down with runtime team.

sara: thanks all. :wave: tagging postmortem next-sprint doc.

incident-bot: Incident PD-83421 transitioned to "stabilized" at 2026-03-15T14:18:00Z.

lucas: closing notes: runbook worked as expected, rollback was fastest path. we should add a canary stage for routing weight rollouts to avoid global oscillation. filing follow-up tickets now.
